binders: An arbitrary type Omega equipped with a measurable-space structure.
An arbitrary measure mu on Omega, together with an instance asserting that mu is a probability measure.
An arbitrary real-valued function X : Omega -> Real.
After the centering hypothesis, an existential real constant C.
Inside the transfer property, arbitrary indices i and j in the five-element condition index type, an implicit real input scale Ki, and an existential real output scale Kj depending on i, j, and Ki.
hypotheses: X is integrable with respect to mu.
The integral of X with respect to mu is exactly zero.
For each invocation of the transfer property, Ki is strictly positive.
For each invocation, the indexed condition LocalDef001(mu,X,i,Ki) holds.
conclusions: There exists a real C with C>=1.
For every pair of the five condition indices i and j and every positive Ki satisfying condition i, there exists a positive Kj such that Kj<=C Ki and condition j holds at Kj.
mathematical_definitions: The five indices select, in exact recursor order, tail (D010), moment growth (D007), bounded square-exponential family (D009), single square-exponential bound (D008), and linear MGF (D006).
Tail at K: X is measurable, K>0, and for every t>=0, mu({|X|>=t}), converted to a real value, is at most 2 exp(-t^2/K^2).
Moment growth at K: X is measurable and almost-everywhere measurable, K>0, and for every real p>=1, |X|^p is integrable with integral at most (K sqrt(p))^p, where exponentiation by p is Real.rpow.
Bounded square-exponential family at K: X is measurable, K>0, and for every real lambda with |lambda|<=1/K, exp(lambda^2 X^2) is integrable with integral at most exp(K^2 lambda^2).
Single square-exponential bound at K: X is measurable, K>0, exp(X^2/K^2) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
Linear MGF at K: X is measurable, K>0, X is integrable with integral zero, and for every real lambda, exp(lambda X) is integrable with integral at most exp(K^2 lambda^2).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every probability space represented by a measurable type Omega and an explicit probability measure mu, and every integrable real function X with mean zero, there is a real comparison factor C>=1 (allowed to depend on Omega, mu, and X) such that any one of the five specified tail, moment, square-exponential, or linear-MGF conditions at any positive scale Ki implies each of the five conditions at some positive scale Kj no larger than C Ki. The output scale Kj may depend on the chosen input condition i, output condition j, and Ki.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The existential C is inside the quantification over Omega, mu, and X, so it may depend on the entire probability space, the measure, and X; the proposition does not assert a universal numerical comparison constant.

The outer assumptions give only integrability and zero integral, not measurability of X. Every indexed condition separately requires measurability, so if X is integrable but not measurable in the pointwise sense used here and no indexed condition is satisfiable, the transfer implication can be vacuously true.
More generally, if no positive Ki satisfies any input indexed condition, every implication in the universal transfer clause is vacuous, and any C>=1 works.
Both the target implication and each indexed predicate repeat positivity requirements: Ki>0 is required outside and again inside condition i; Kj>0 is required outside and again inside condition j.
The moment formulation quantifies over all real p>=1 and uses Real.rpow, rather than quantifying only over natural or integer moments.
The bounded square-exponential formulation is exactly restricted to |lambda|<=1/K and integrates exp(lambda^2 X^2); this is not a statement about exp(lambda X).
The linear MGF formulation itself repeats integrability and zero-mean conditions already assumed outside, while the other four formulations do not internally require zero mean.
The tail probability is expressed via Measure.real, i.e. conversion of the extended-nonnegative-real measure to a real; finiteness is ensured in the intended probability-measure setting.
The theorem asserts existence but neither optimality nor a fixed value of C or Kj, and Kj may vary with i, j, and Ki.
